https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Trump says U.S. won’t attack Iran before midterm elections
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
U.S. President Donald Trump said in a social media post that the U.S. would “not be attacking Iran” before November’s midterm elections, citing what he said were “productive discussions” with the Islamic Republic.

The president’s comments on Thursday amounted to an unusual blending of national security issues and domestic politics. His decision to lay off on new strikes comes despite Iran escalating attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran-backed militants in Yemen attacking energy facilities in Saudi Arabia and the president’s decision to move U.S. bombers from a base in the U.K. because of possible Iran-linked threats.

The remarks follow recent reporting in the Atlantic that Trump was mulling plans to strike Iran before the midterm contests and that the White House had asked the Pentagon to prepare options. The New York Times separately reported Thursday that senior White House national security officials recently discussed plans that included an intense three-day campaign.

Trump said in an interview with Time magazine published earlier this month that ramped-up military strikes against Iran were “possible” following the elections.

Late last month, the Pentagon deployed an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and marines to the Persian Gulf, a U.S. official previously said. That move bolsters the two aircraft carriers already in the region and gives American commanders more options if Trump chooses to launch new attacks on Iran, the official said.

Trump has suggested Iran was waiting to see how his Republican Party would do during the midterms.

In September, he explicitly dismissed the relevance of the vote when it came to the Iran war.

“I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election when it comes to Iran,” Trump said. “It doesn’t even enter my mind.”

In his Thursday post, the president did not offer any details about the discussions he said were happening with Iran. Talks have remained deadlocked over a host of issues, including control of the vital Strait of Hormuz. The president rejected an Iranian offer after holding discussions via mediators during United Nations meetings in September.

Trump has repeatedly cited productive or ongoing diplomatic talks with Iran without any results. He’s also repeatedly threatened military escalation against Tehran, sometimes without ordering new attacks. Trump added on Thursday that a U.S. naval blockade of Iranian exports would remain in place.

Yet fresh tanker attacks by Iran threaten to curtail a recent uptick in oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz: U.K. Maritime Trade Operations reported nine attacks in the waterway so far in October.

And while oil shipments through Hormuz are approaching prewar levels with the U.S. military’s assistance, the recent spate of Iranian attacks have already helped trigger another surge in oil prices.

The U.S. has moved its B-1B bombers from the Royal Air Force base in Fairford, Britain, citing terror threats.

The base had been used by the U.S. in its bombing campaign against Iran earlier in the conflict, but the warplanes were hastily removed following the arrests of a number of men outside the base. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said it’s likely Iran was involved in the plot, with Trump saying the bombers were removed to lower the security risks.

British officials said they’re concerned Trump’s decision will embolden Tehran and Moscow to use more proxies to carry out sabotage attacks. European officials are already struggling to contend with a Russian campaign of what is known as hybrid warfare attacks across the continent, with attempted attacks in Germany and elsewhere.

Back in the Middle East, the Iran-backed Houthi militant group in Yemen also struck two airports in neighboring Saudi Arabia in the past two days, killing three people and injuring dozens more, in a blow to one of Washington’s key partners in the Middle East.

The U.S. is currently opting out of taking a direct role in a Saudi-backed counter-offensive to take back Houthi-claimed territory, but Saudi Arabia’s allies could come under pressure to become more involved as ballistic missiles are fired toward Riyadh.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Trump said in a social media post that the U.S. would ‘not be attacking Iran’s Iran before November’S. midterm elections. The president’ed his comments on Thursday amounted to an unusual blending of national security issues and domestic politics.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2026/1.title: Tokyo walks away with two spots on 50 Best Bars list
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2026/1.author: Weiwen Lin
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2026/1.text:
Tokyo had two bars on The 50 Best Bars 2026 list, announced in Milan on Wednesday.

The awards list was renamed from World’s 50 Best Bars last month, with “The 50” serving as the master brand.

Tokyo had one fewer bar on the list than last year. The rankings also fell: Bar Benfiddich dropped from No. 18 to No. 44, while Virtu slipped from No. 45 to No. 48. The Bellwood, which debuted at No. 48 last year, sneaked onto the extended 51-100 list at No. 100.

Hong Kong’s Bar Leone took the top spot for the second consecutive year, reinforcing its reputation as a force to be reckoned with.

With four bars on the list, Hong Kong also reclaimed its status as Asia’s leading cocktail destination from Tokyo. Bangkok, the top regional performer in the Asian edition of the awards in July, followed closely with three bars: Bar Us ranked No. 4, Dry Wave Cocktail Studio debuted at No. 27 and BKK Social Club landed at No. 30. Singapore placed two bars, tying with Tokyo.

Shingo Gokan, founder of bar consultancy SG Group and bartender at The SG Club in Tokyo, received the Roku Industry Icon Award for pioneering a new era of Asian cocktail culture through his international venues, including Speak Low in Shanghai and Sip & Guzzle in New York.

This year’s list features bars from 26 cities, with 14 new entries.

In a press statement, Faye Hugget, director of community for The 50 Best Bars, said this year’s rankings are “a powerful reflection of the extraordinary talent, dedication and hospitality that continue to elevate bar culture around the world.”
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/life/2026/1.summary: Tokyo had two bars on The 50 Best Bars 2026 list, announced in Milan on Wednesday. Hong Kong's Bar Leone took the top spot for the second consecutive year. Hong Hong Kong also reclaimed its status as Asia’s leading cocktail destination from Tokyo.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.title: Adrian Bianco championed Japan’s underground culture
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.author: Ora Margolis
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
Speaking to The Japan Times in August 2024, Adrian Bianco, editor in chief of digital platform Sabukaru Online, said he fell in love with “the beauty of the ordinary” in Japan.

But through Sabukaru, Bianco, who died at 40 after an unexpected accident on Aug. 17, brought his readers something decidedly less ordinary: the underground culture, fashion and creative scenes he documented in Japan and across Asia. Sabukaru was part of Bianco Bianco, a Tokyo-based media collective he founded that also includes Gata Magazine, a publication focused on dark avant-garde fashion.

Bianco also founded the Berlin-based creative agency neronero and Sabukaru Showroom, an annual Paris pop-up supporting emerging brands including Jian Ye, Luca Hamers and Alivefrom. He was also a shareholder of Arys Store, a Berlin clothing shop specializing in functional wear.

NSS Magazine described Bianco as “less as a publisher and more as a mentor and cultural connector,” praising his ability to spot talent before it gained wider attention and give visibility to people on the margins of mainstream culture.

Bianco was born in Munich on May 21, 1986, as Adrian Hans Eckehard Heinrich Weiss. He later adopted the surname Bianco, the Italian translation of Weiss, meaning “white.”

After dropping out of law school at the University of Regensburg, he worked at a Berlin sneaker shop and ran a popular blog about sneaker culture and the broader world of 2010s Hypebeast fashion. The blog led to work with Vice Media Group, first at its creative agency Virtue and later as a senior digital creative at Vice.

At Vice, Bianco developed a social-first approach to youth culture journalism, adapting the visual language of print and web magazines to platforms such as Snapchat, Instagram and YouTube. He later brought that approach to Sabukaru.

After repeated visits to Tokyo for market research and agency projects, Bianco moved to Japan full time in 2019. “I always wanted to move to Japan or somewhere else in Asia, but it seemed like an impossible task,” he told The Japan Times in 2024. “I basically left my whole life behind and started from zero.”

What began, in Bianco’s words, as a “three-meter square” office in Shimbashi grew into a multistory operation near Shimokitazawa. In 2025, Sabukaru expanded beyond its online presence with an annual print edition.

Bianco Bianco and its publications, Sabukaru Online and Gata Magazine, remain in operation. Bianco is survived by his business co-founder, former girlfriend and later friend Marta Espinosa, his mother and his sister.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.title: Anime is winning over a new generation of fans
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.author: Sohee Kim
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
Anime is taking up more entertainment time among Gen Z and teenage fans globally, stoking a broader cultural appetite for related merchandise, games and manga.

Across 10 countries surveyed, 79% of anime fans between the ages of 13 and 17 said they’re watching more anime than a year ago. Meanwhile, 68% of Gen Zers said the same, according to new findings for Sony Group Corp.’s anime streaming platform Crunchyroll conducted by the National Research Group, a strategy consultancy.

Aided by the rise of international streaming platforms such as Netflix Inc. and Crunchyroll, which has about 21 million paid subscribers, anime connected with new audiences across the globe during the pandemic. More than half of Netflix’s members now regularly watch anime. Crunchyroll estimates that roughly 1.6 billion people outside Japan and China have some interest in anime.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: South Korea test-fires its first homegrown hypersonic weapon: presidency
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
SEOUL – South Korea test-fired its first homegrown hypersonic weapon on Thursday, the presidential office said, days after Pyongyang announced the AI-assisted launch of an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung “observed the first test launch of a hypersonic glide vehicle (HGV) — currently under research and development using domestic technology,” the presidential Blue House said in a statement.

Hypersonic glide vehicles are sent into the upper atmosphere via rocket boosters or on ballistic missiles, then glide towards their target at five times the speed of sound or greater.

Hailing a “key strategic asset capable of changing the course of the battlefield,” the South Korean statement said that the missiles’ “unpredictable flight trajectories and overwhelming speed enable them to strike key strategic targets.”

The test was aimed at verifying “the performance of ultra-high-temperature heat-resistant materials — a core technology for glide vehicles — as well as guidance and control capabilities and the ability to fly irregularly at low altitudes under hypersonic flight conditions,” it added.

Analysts say North Korea, which is technically at war with the South, has stepped up testing of its own hypersonic weapons with technological support from Russia.

In response, “South Korea has also been devoting considerable effort to developing the technology — and can be said to have achieved a successful test this time,” said Hong Sung-pyo, senior researcher at the Seoul-based Korea Institute for Military Affairs.

Moscow has used hypersonic missiles in combat since around 2024, according to analysts.

Pyongyang has said its Saturday launch involved the use of AI, claiming there was “no way to avoid” the missile that was “capable of changing its flight orbit at a low altitude.”

It also said that the missile’s “wave-like trajectory mode” left South Korea and Japan unable to track it effectively.

Both Seoul and Washington have said the missile could be “sufficiently detected and intercepted using the defensive assets possessed by the two allies.”

South Korea said that the hypersonic glide vehicle tested Thursday “descended to a low altitude after separation, freely altered its trajectory both vertically and horizontally, and ... accurately struck its designated target.”

The weapon offered “a new deterrence capability capable of striking key targets within the Korean Peninsula’s operational environment,” the Blue House said.

The test was aimed at verifying “the performance of ultra-high-temperature heat-resistant materials’s performance’ The weapon offered “a new deterrence capability capable of striking key targets within the Korean Peninsula’

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: BOJ raises economic assessment for Tohoku and Shikoku as tech demand remains strong
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
The Bank of Japan revised up its economic assessment for two of the country’s nine regions in a quarterly report released Thursday while leaving it unchanged for the rest.

The central bank compiled the report at the day’s meeting of managers of its regional branches, which was held at its headquarters in Tokyo. Demand related to artificial intelligence remained strong, including for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and electronic components. When it comes to production, the BOJ raised its economic assessment for seven of the nine regions, excluding Hokkaido and the Tokai region.

In the report, the BOJ said the economy in all nine regions has been “picking up moderately,” “recovering moderately,” or “on a moderate recovery trend” while noting that “some weakness has been seen in part.”

The central bank revised upward its economic assessment for the Tohoku region from the assessment that the economy “has been picking up” to the view that the economy “has been recovering moderately.” It also raised its economic view for Shikoku from an assessment that the economy “has been picking up moderately” to the view that the economy “has been picking up.”

In interviews with companies, an electrical equipment maker in Osaka said that AI-related demand has been increasing faster than expected and that robust demand is likely to continue for about the next three years.

Many branch chiefs reported that private consumption has generally remained resilient, supported by improvements in real income. A department store operator in Shizuoka Prefecture said that sales of high-priced goods, such as luxury watches and jewelry, remained strong. Against the backdrop of rising stock prices, there were also reports that sales to wealthy consumers showed no signs of weakening.

Meanwhile, a retailer in Nagoya said that bad weather, including typhoons and heavy rain, weighed on consumption.

Kenji Fujita, manager of the central bank’s branch in Osaka, said at a news conference that small and midsize companies have made relatively smooth progress in passing on higher costs in business-to-business transactions, but that the process is still only halfway along and uneven among businesses closer to consumers.

Regarding the impact of the BOJ’s interest rate hikes to date, an official at the central bank’s Research and Statistics Department said only some companies had indicated that they would put off capital investment, while many said they would make necessary investments, including in labor-saving measures.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: The Bank of Japan revised up its economic assessment for two of the country's nine regions. The central bank compiled the report at the day’s meeting of managers of its regional branches. Demand related to artificial intelligence remained strong, including for semiconductor manufacturing equipment and electronic components.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Germany arrests member of Qilin hacker group who was extradited from Japan
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
A Russian national believed to be a key member of the notorious Qilin international hacker group was arrested by German authorities after being extradited from Japan, Japanese police said Thursday.

According to the National Police Agency, German authorities had obtained an arrest warrant for the 28-year-old Russian citizen on suspicion of extortion for allegedly attacking German companies and demanding cryptocurrency payments.

After learning that he planned to visit Japan as a tourist in May, the agency’s cyber special investigation department identified his whereabouts through a joint investigation involving the Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto police departments.

He was detained at a hotel in Osaka that month and handed over to German authorities this month following a decision by the Tokyo High Court under the extradition law.

Qilin has launched ransomware attacks worldwide since October 2022, affecting about 4,000 companies. It demands ransom payments to restore encrypted data and threatens to release stolen data if victims refuse to pay.

Since April 2023, it has hit 53 companies, hospitals and schools in Japan. The group claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on Asahi Group Holdings in 2025.

Qilin operates through numerous affiliates that carry out cyber intrusions and extortion attempts using ransomware provided by core members responsible for malware development and system management.

“It was significant that we identified and arrested a (Qilin) member through international cooperation,” a senior NPA official said.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: German authorities arrest Russian national believed to be a key member of the notorious Qilin international hacker group. He was arrested by German authorities after being extradited from Japan. Qil in has launched ransomware attacks worldwide since October 2022.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Nihon Hidankyo hears calls to pass cause to second generation
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
Nihon Hidankyo, a Japanese atomic bomb survivor organization, heard calls Thursday for children of atomic bomb survivors to carry on its movement as it weighs whether to remain active or disband.

About 80 hibakusha survivors of the 1945 atomic bombings and other representatives of constituent groups from across Japan attended the meeting in Tokyo.

They reported their views on the future of the organization, formally known as the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers Organizations.

A group from Hiroshima, where the nuclear attack took place on Aug. 6, 1945, said Nihon Hidankyo received the 2024 Nobel Peace Prize in recognition of its efforts to spread awareness of the realities of the atomic bombings, and argued that “disbanding would have a major impact.” It said that the organization should remain active, centered on second-generation hibakusha.

A group from Nagasaki, which was attacked with an atomic bomb on Aug. 9, 1945, said it was still discussing the issue but that some viewed disbanding as “out of the question.”

A group from Kanagawa Prefecture, meanwhile, said disbanding would be realistic once hibakusha are no longer active, while arguing that the movement itself should be passed on.

Some other groups said they were still weighing their options.

The organization’s committee representing second-generation hibakusha also presented its views. The members said second-generation hibakusha are also “victims of the atomic bombings,” having grown up witnessing their parents’ suffering and living with anxieties of their own.

“We want to keep Nihon Hidankyo going together with our supporters and carry on its movement,” they said.

Nihon Hidankyo will decide its final policy at its regular general meeting in June next year.

About 80 hibakusha survivors of the 1945 atomic bombings attended the meeting in Tokyo. The group is formally known as the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Trump reportedly asked Xi to meet with Takaichi
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
HONG KONG – U.S. President Donald Trump asked Chinese President Xi Jinping at their summit last month to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Hong Kong’s South China Morning Post reported Thursday.

Xi was not receptive to the proposal, according to the paper.

During the last U.S.-China summit in Washington, Trump expressed concern that China’s restrictions on rare earth exports to Japan were also affecting U.S. industries, adding that this situation indirectly violates the U.S.-China trade truce.

Xi responded that China-Japan relations should be separate from China-U.S. relations. He also claimed that the risk of a resurgence of Japanese militarism is growing.

The newspaper also reported that the Japanese government has requested a bilateral summit with China on the occasion of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen next month.

However, China suggested that, instead of Xi, Premier Li Qiang, the second-ranking official in the Chinese Communist Party, would meet with Takaichi. Japan responded cautiously to this offer, according to the report.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Trump asked Chinese President Xi Jinping at their summit to hold a bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Xi was not receptive to the proposal, according to the paper.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
STOCKHOLM – Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson ⁠won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature,” the award-giving body said on Thursday.

“She was very taken by ‌surprise. We ‌didn’t have so much time to speak, and all she had time ​to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she’s listening to the wind,” said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Swedish Academy.

Canadian ‌poet and essayist Carson’s work often blends verse, prose, ​dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix. Born in Toronto, she has also held Icelandic citizenship since 2022.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.title: Climate needs same urgency as defense spending, COP31 chief says
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.author: Ishika Mookerjee
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.text:
Action to curb emissions and bolster resilience to the impacts of extreme weather needs similar urgency to international efforts to lift defense investments, according to the head of next month’s annual global climate change conference.

“The same responsibility, same determination, we expect each and every country to show in climate action,” Murat Kurum, Turkey’s environment minister and president-designate of the COP31 summit, told reporters Thursday in Fiji at preparatory talks ahead of the November event. “What does it mean to spend 5% for defense if you don’t have a country to live on? What does it mean to defend it?”

North Atlantic Treaty Organization nations last year committed to spend at least 3.5% of national economic output on core defense programs, and as much as a further 1.5% on related areas by 2035. In contrast, the European Union has warned “there is no scope” for new climate finance commitments at COP31, according to a draft document.

The flow of finance to fund work to lower emissions or for climate adaptation projects is faltering as nations cut overall aid budgets, and following the withdrawal of the U.S. from efforts focused on global warming. Spending on the issue by Germany, Europe’s biggest economy, fell last year and the nation missed a pledge on climate financing.

Nations “must deliver on existing finance commitments,” and continue to advance a goal of delivering $1.3 trillion a year to developing countries by 2035, Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, said at the Fiji event.

“This is what COP31 can and must do, help convert promises into more real-world results,” Stiell said. “That depends on many factors, including scaling up, speeding up, and broadening access to affordable climate finance.”

The Pre-COP talks in Fiji have won some new pledges, including for the Pacific Resilience Facility, a mechanism established last year to direct financing for climate and disaster projects to vulnerable nations in the region. Fiji’s government offered $10 million and will press nations at the COP talks to “get climate finance into the hands of the people who really need it,” said Lynda Tabuya, the country’s minister for information, environment and climate change.

The U.K. pledged $13 million to the Pacific facility, the Netherlands offered $1.12 million and Denmark and Ireland both doubled previous commitments, according to a statement. Australia, which previously pledged 100 million Australian dollars ($70 million) to the resilience fund, made separate proposals this week totaling about AU$10 million for renewable energy projects in the Pacific and to protect infrastructure in the region.

However, the Pacific fund, which aims to build disaster preparedness without furthering the debt for participating countries, is yet to meet an initial target to win commitments of $500 million by the end of the year, and to hit a longer-term target for $1.5 billion.

With limited prospects for major new climate financing, organizers of the COP31 talks are focusing on work to improve access for developing countries — including in the Pacific, Caribbean and Indian Ocean — to already existing funding, and will seek new support from development banks and other countries.

“The countries that need the finance the most get it the least,” Australian Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen, who will serve as COP31 president of negotiations, said in Fiji. “That has got to change.”

Bowen and Kurum on Tuesday led a delegation of dignitaries, including the heads of the Asian Development Bank and Green Climate Fund, to visit climate change-threatened Tuvalu in the western Pacific Ocean.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/environment.summary: The European Union has warned “there is no scope’ for new climate finance commitments at COP31. The flow of finance to fund work to lower emissions or for climate adaptation projects is faltering as nations cut overall aid budgets. The United Nations must deliver on existing finance commitments, says Simon Stiell.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Samsung and TSMC fail to excite investors used to torrid AI growth
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Yoolim Lee
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Samsung Electronics earned a nearly ninefold rise in quarterly operating profit, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.’s sales jumped 51%, reflecting the spoils of relentless spending on AI infrastructure.

Yet investor reaction to a day of record-setting results was muted, weighed down by worries about the staying power of an investment boom propped up by rising debt levels. Samsung’s stock price shed 2.4% Thursday in Seoul. In Tokyo, shares of both companies’ suppliers including Tokyo Electron, Advantest and Ibiden declined.

Investors are questioning how long AI spending can last, especially as companies’ big capex plans come under pressure because of rising borrowing costs around the world.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Uniqlo on track to overtake H&M, eyes Zara for global No. 1
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Yui Hasebe
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Uniqlo owner Fast Retailing Co.’s annual revenue climbed 17% to a record ¥3.96 trillion ($25 billion), putting it solidly on a path to pull ahead of H&M as the world’s No. 2 apparel retailer and challenge Zara for the top spot.

The sales milestone underscores Fast Retailing’s ascent among global high-street fashion retailers, with sales set to surpass Hennes & Mauritz, which is projected by analysts to post sales of 222.7 billion kronor ($22.3 billion) for its fiscal year through November, while narrowing the gap with Zara owner Industria de Diseno Textil.

The latest results show how far Uniqlo has come from its origins as a low-price Japanese casual-wear chain to become an international brand built around functional all-season apparel, as it pushes deeper into North America and Europe. Even so, Fast Retailing founder and Chief Executive Officer Tadashi Yanai still needs to more than double annual sales to reach his long-term target and build the global apparel powerhouse he has long envisioned.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: South Korea to recall ambassador from Ukraine amid deepening row
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
SEOUL – South Korea said Thursday it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine in response to a deepening diplomatic row over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul.

The decision comes as the two countries have been at loggerheads since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sparked anger in Seoul by disclosing the transfer of the prisoners, who were captured on the battlefield early last year.

It also follows a report this week alleging that more than 176,000 metric tons of fuel, mostly diesel, had been shipped from South Korea to Russia in July and August, sparking accusations Seoul was helping alleviate Russian fuel shortages.

“The government has decided to recall its ambassador to Ukraine,” the foreign ministry said in a statement.

“The government hopes that all outstanding issues between the two countries will be resolved amicably and will continue consultations with the Ukrainian side to that end.”

Seoul has summoned Kyiv’s ambassador and threatened unspecified “further measures,” while South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has demanded an official apology over concerns that the disclosure could put the POWs’ families at risk.

Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga has referred to the incident as a “diplomatic misunderstanding“.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author

Authorities are calling for renewed vigilance against cybersecurity threats after the disclosure of a flurry of incidents exposing users’ personal data, and as early figures show Japan may be headed for an unusually bad year for corporate data breaches.

With reported cases up, methods used by bad actors evolving, and artificial intelligence lowering barriers for would-be scammers, growing attention on the threat and new laws that allow more preemptive measures are in focus — but will they be enough?

The targets of recent cyberattacks have ranged from restaurants and retailers to media groups and research institutions, with few sectors left unscathed. Experts say those cases may be just the tip of the iceberg.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Nomura and Daiwa CEOs flag risk that AI may spoil stock market rally
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Takashi Nakamichi
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Japan’s two largest securities firms expect the country’s stock market rally to extend well into 2027, even as a potential reversal in artificial intelligence investment looms as the primary threat.

“Markets, stock prices and corporate earnings are all being driven very strongly by investment in AI,” Nomura Holdings CEO Kentaro Okuda said at a Nikkei event in Tokyo on Thursday. “If sentiment toward AI were to shift and that trend went into reverse, I think that could pose a significant risk.”

Akihiko Ogino, CEO of smaller rival Daiwa Securities Group, made similar remarks on the same panel.

Both executives projected the Nikkei 225 Stock Average to reach 80,000, though their paths diverged: Ogino set that target for this year, while Okuda placed the index at about 75,000 by year-end and above 80,000 by end-2027. The gauge closed at 69,042.11 on Thursday.

Their remarks reflect confidence in a near four-year boom in Japanese equities, which are trading close to a record as AI investment, corporate governance reforms and a return to inflation encourage investors. The rally has also fueled earnings at the two securities firms, with both posting record profits last fiscal year.

Ogino said he expects the Nikkei to reach 88,000 toward the end of 2027, and that the yen would trade at about ¥160 per dollar through that period. Okuda projected the Japanese currency at about ¥156 per dollar at year-end, with a gradual strengthening thereafter as geopolitical concerns ease.

Ogino attributed the yen’s recent recovery from excessive weakness to joint intervention, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s calls for the Bank of Japan to raise rates, and the central bank’s September hike. He described rising rates as a “positive development” that reflected economic growth.

Okuda said overseas investors retained strong interest in Japan and that the negative impact of higher rates had not been significant so far. He added that conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine may be prolonged, potentially pushing up energy prices and disrupting supply chains.

Both executives pointed to the possibility that recent public opposition to AI and data centers in countries including the U.S. would lead to a drop in investment in the sector.

“The biggest concern is how market participants will respond,” Ogino said. “They can change their views dramatically over a very short period of time, causing sharp swings in asset prices. Those market moves can amplify the impact of a risk far beyond what is happening in the real economy. I think that is the biggest challenge.”
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: Japan's two largest securities firms expect the country's stock market rally to extend well into 2027. The Nikkei 225 Stock Average is expected to reach 80,000 by year-end and above 80,00 by end-2027. Both executives said the rally has fueled earnings at the two securities firms.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Osaka’s Midosuji inks sister-street pact with Paris’ Champs-Elysees
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
PARIS – A signing ceremony was held in France on Wednesday for a sister-street partnership between Midosuji, the main street in Osaka, and the Avenue des Champs-Elysees, a famous tourist attraction in Paris.

The ceremony in Paris was attended by Osaka Mayor Hideyuki Yokoyama, who signed a memorandum on the partnership, under which the two sides pledge to cooperate in reorganizing road space and creating attractive urban environments to develop people-centered streets.

In his speech, Yokoyama said that Midosuji will mark its 90th anniversary next year, adding, “As we look toward the 100th anniversary, we hope to create a rich space where people can relax, while learning from the people of the Champs-Elysees.”

Referring to the 2025 World Exposition in Osaka, Yokoyama said that the six-month event achieved tremendous success, with the France Pavilion helping generate excitement at the venue, despite criticism before its opening.

Marc-Antoine Jamet of the Champs-Elysees committee, the promotional organization that signed the memorandum, said that the two streets share a common commitment to bringing a human touch to their public spaces and expressed hope for exchanges through events and other activities.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.summary: Osaka Mayor Hideyuki Yokoyama signs memorandum on sister-street partnership. The two streets share a common commitment to bringing human touch to their public spaces.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Prudential Japan executives take pay cuts over staff misconduct
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Taiga Uranaka
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Top executives at Prudential Financial’s Japan unit will take pay cuts after a panel of outside experts issued a report on widespread employee misconduct involving customers’ money.

President Hiromitsu Tokumaru and two others will take a 30% reduction in compensation for three months to take responsibility for the matter, the company said in a statement on Thursday. The investigative committee found that issues at the unit of the U.S. insurance group, Prudential Life, stemmed from structural problems in its governance framework and business model.

The case is the latest in a series of scandals to hit Japan’s insurance industry in recent years, undermining confidence at a time when households are looking to invest more of their savings. The country’s financial regulator is considering penalizing Prudential Life with measures including a temporary business suspension order, according to a person with knowledge of the matter.

Prudential Life established the committee after disclosing alleged misconduct by more than 100 current and former sales employees that caused more than ¥3.1 billion ($20 million) in customer losses. Cases ranged from staff pitching fictitious investments to borrowing money from clients.

Evaluation and compensation systems reinforced incentives to prioritize short-term results, the company said in the statement. The company will revise these to encourage behavior that emphasizes long-term customer relationships, compliance and sound sales practices, it said.

Prudential Life has voluntarily halted new life insurance sales since February to focus on overhauling its governance and sales practices. It extended the initial 90-day suspension until early November, saying it needed more time to complete the reforms.

Prudential Life, which began operations in Japan in 1988, has carved out a niche in a market long dominated by domestic players including Nippon Life Insurance and Daiichi Life Group. It relies on a relatively small sales force known as “life planners,” who target affluent customers including business owners and doctors and offer highly tailored products and financial planning services.

Traditional Japanese insurers, by contrast, employ much larger sales forces that have historically sold more standardized products through community-based, face-to-face networks.

Prudential’s sales representatives built a reputation for aggressive selling. At a news conference in January, company executives said a compensation structure heavily dependent on commissions had distorted incentives and contributed to breaches of internal rules.

In its annual policy priorities released in September, the Financial Services Agency said it would “take rigorous supervisory action” against misconduct by insurance companies.

Three years ago, authorities penalized the country’s largest property-and-casualty insurers for colluding on insurance premiums for corporate clients. More recently, employees of several major life insurers were found to have mishandled data.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Takaichi says economy doesn’t need reflationary policy
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Akemi Terukina
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Japan no longer needs policy to stimulate inflation as the economy isn’t in a state of deflation anymore, echoing a comment made recently by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

“Japan’s economy is no longer at a stage where it needs reflationary policies with monetary easing and fiscal expansion,” Takaichi said in response to questions in parliament Thursday. Her policy “differs from so-called reflationary policy,” she said.

Takaichi’s government has sent a series of signals lately that it is moving beyond reflationary policy, following Bessent’s remarks that Japan should leave efforts to reflate the economy behind. Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda also said last month that the central bank’s policy phase has shifted, with more focus now needed on upside price risks.

Takaich's government has sent a series of signals lately that it is moving beyond reflationary policy.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: Bankruptcies linked to labor shortages in Japan climb in first half of fiscal year
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
The number of corporate bankruptcies in Japan caused by labor shortages has risen 17% from the previous year.

The figure reached 240 for the first half of the fiscal year, April to September, the highest level since comparable data became available in fiscal 2013, Tokyo Shoko Research said on Thursday.

Of them, failures stemming from soaring labor costs climbed nearly twofold to 130.

About 60% of bankruptcies caused by labor shortages occurred at businesses with less than ¥10 million ($63,000) in capital.

“Pressure to raise wages weighed on the finances of small and midsize companies,” a Tokyo Shoko Research official said.

The total number of bankruptcies in the first half of the fiscal year rose 3.8% to 5,373, a 13-year high for the period. The data covered failures with liabilities of at least ¥10 million.

Failures caused by rising prices rose 17.8% to 436, while those related to failures in finding a successor jumped 23.4% to a record high of 263.

By industry, services firms, including restaurants and hotels, made up the largest share of bankruptcies, at 1,828, up 3.7%.

Total liabilities left by bankruptcies grew 23.5% to ¥856 billion because of an increase in large-scale bankruptcies including the failure of Zentoshin, a credit card payment processing service firm.

In September alone, the total number of bankruptcies fell 4.8% to 831. Liabilities dropped 3.1% to ¥108.9 billion.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: The number of corporate bankruptcies in Japan has risen 17% from the previous year. The figure reached 240 for the first half of the fiscal year, April to September. Of them, failures stemming from soaring labor costs climbed nearly twofold to 130.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.title: Elvis comes back as a ghost in a noh theater play
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.author: Kenji Kurabayashi
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.text:
The king of rock ’n’ roll, Elvis Presley, has had many reimaginings in popular culture, but Japanese noh theater might be one of his most unexpected contexts yet. Nonetheless his ghost will be on stage in Tokyo on Oct. 10 and 11.

Theatre Nohgaku will bring its original noh play “Blue Moon Over Memphis” to the sophomore edition of Autumn Meteorite Tokyo, one of Japan’s largest performing arts festivals that takes place at the Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre in Ikebukuro. Although the play was previously performed at Waseda University’s Okuma Auditorium and Kyoto’s Kongo Noh Theatre in 2024 and at Tokyo’s Kita Noh Theatre in 2025, Autumn Meteorite contextualizes the work in the constellation of world theater and brings it to wider audiences. This time, the venue will be a contemporary theater stage instead of a traditional noh stage with four pillars and the show is just one of the festival’s international offerings.

“Blue Moon,” slated for the festival’s opening weekend, is a prime example of the artistic possibilities of cross-cultural exchange.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/culture/202.summary: The play will be on stage in Tokyo on Oct. 10 and 11. The play was previously performed at Waseda University’s Okuma Auditorium and Kyoto’'s Kongo Noh Theatre in 2024.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.title: Jayden Daniels vow to ‘embrace the brace’ in return from latest elbow injury
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.text:
Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was a full participant in practice Wednesday, another step toward his return from a left elbow injury.

Daniels hurt his non-throwing arm on the final play of the first half in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys and traveled with the Commanders (1-3) to London last week. He was limited in every practice before the loss to the Indianapolis Colts, when starter Marcus Mariota went down with a sprained knee.

Rookie Athan Kaliakmanis replaced Mariota, but Daniels took the reps in Wednesday’s practice. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed he plans to start Daniels this week against the visiting New York Giants (3-1), barring any setbacks.

“The goal is for him to have a full week of practice and start on Sunday,” Quinn said. “We won’t put him out there before he’s ready.”

Part of getting ready was beginning work in Wednesday’s practice on protecting his elbow. Quinn said there are some adjustments for Daniels to make and others for the team to address.

Daniels wore a brace on his left elbow and plans to keep it on for the game.

“I’m gonna embrace the brace,” Daniels said. “Go out there and be the best version of myself.”

Daniels, 25, missed time last season with the same injury and was forced to exit his first game back in 2025 after spraining the same elbow. He played a total of only seven games last season due to multiple injuries.

He has completed only 57% of his passes this season (29 of 51) but has three touchdowns and no turnovers in six quarters of game action in 2026. He is 3-0 in his career against the Giants.

“Just putting in the countless hours of work and preparation,” Daniels said. “Just go out there and give myself the best opportunity to perform to the best of my ability on Sunday.”

The Commanders hosted former United Football League MVP quarterback Jack Plummer on Wednesday morning, according to the league transactions log.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was a full participant in practice Wednesday. Daniels hurt his left elbow on the final play of the first half in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys. He was limited in every practice before the loss to the Indianapolis Colts.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.title: Naomi Osaka among stars to commit to Australian Open ‘1 Point Slam’
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2026.text:
MELBOURNE – The Australian Open will revive its innovative “1 Point Slam” in 2027 with Carlos Alcaraz, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Jannik Sinner among those agreeing to take part Thursday.

The sudden-death contest was played for the first time at Melbourne Park this year ahead of the opening Grand Slam of the season, pitting 24 professionals alongside 24 amateurs and celebrity wildcards.

Each match consisted of just one point — win and you advanced, lose and you were out.

Against the odds, amateur Jordan Smith sensationally upset the star-studded field at a packed Rod Laver Arena to collect the prize of 1 million Australian dollars ($670,000).

“It creates an opportunity for grassroots tennis players to share the spotlight with some of the biggest names in the game,” said Tennis Australia’s Tom Larner.

“Having stars like Carlos Alcaraz, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Jannik Sinner locked in to play, alongside everyday Australians ... captures exactly what this event is about, bringing people together through tennis.”

The amateur field will again comprise winners of eight state championship rounds played across Australia, along with eight others who come through qualifying.

More than 1.3 million fans attended the 2026 Australian Open, and organisers are planning to increase viewing capacity and seating even further for the 2027 tournament which runs from January 17 to 31.

The sudden-death contest was played for the first time at Melbourne Park this year.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: U.S. opens direct talks with Myanmar’s generals, reversing years of isolation
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: Simon Lewis
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
WASHINGTON – The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has begun direct talks with Myanmar’s military-installed government, according to U.S. officials and others familiar with the outreach, in a sharp reversal of Washington’s efforts to isolate the country’s generals following the 2021 coup.

The U.S. assistant secretary of state for intelligence and research, Michael Vance, played a leading role in the outreach, which has focused on shutting down scam centers that target Americans but could lead to broader engagement, including on Myanmar’s rare-earth mineral deposits, according to seven current and former officials and others familiar with the policy shift.

Vance joined talks with coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing in the capital Naypyitaw on Sept. 15-16. The meeting was aimed at securing the release of American businessman Adam Castillo but also provided an opening for further engagement, four of the people said.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/commentary/.title: The West wants newcomers on its own terms. So does Japan.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/commentary/.author: Waka Ikeda
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/commentary/.text:
Having lived in the United States and Japan for many years and now in Hungary, I have felt the societal rules most sharply in Japan, where origin, schooling and manners are read and weighed, even among Japanese.

But that is only part of the story. Japan is widening the door for temporary foreign workers while narrowing the path to permanent residency. For all the talk of anti-immigrant sentiment, there were a record 2.57 million foreign workers in Japan at the end of October 2025, up 11.7% in a year.

That is not simply exclusion. It is selection, and it is happening across the rich world. The question is whether a country that guards its way of life through strict rules can still attract the workers and talent it increasingly needs.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/commentary/.summary: Japan is widening the door for temporary foreign workers while narrowing the path to permanent residency. There were a record 2.57 million foreign workers in Japan at the end of October 2025, up 11.7% in a year.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.title: Nobel winner Kenso Soai says he understood the significance of his research
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: Tomoko Otake
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
Japanese scientist Kenso Soai, one of two winners of Wednesday’s Nobel Prize in Chemistry, knew the significance of his research all along — though he had not expected that he would ever get the coveted prize, let alone this year.

When he received a phone call from the Nobel Foundation in Sweden notifying him of the prize a few hours before the announcement, he was out shopping for groceries at a supermarket near his home in Shiki, Saitama Prefecture.

“I may sound arrogant, but I had thought I would not get complaints if I won,” Soai, 76, told a news conference on Wednesday night at the Tokyo University of Science, where he taught and researched until he retired in 2016.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/1.text:
NEW DELHI – A corridor named after the late former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe has been completed at an international convention center built with Japanese grant aid in the Hindu holy city of Varanasi in the northern Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

Attending a ceremony Wednesday to mark the completion, Abe’s widow, Akie, said that if her husband were alive, he would have been moved by the creation of a corridor bearing his name and would have come to see it firsthand, according to local media reports.

Photos displayed on the wall of the Abe Memorial Corridor include one showing the former prime minister holding a meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In a post on social media platform X, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that the corridor symbolizes Abe’s contributions to strengthening historical, cultural and diplomatic ties between India and Japan.

Abe visited Varanasi in 2015 while serving as prime minister.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: AI data-center boom ignites bidding war for critical TDK unit
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: Takashi Mochizuki
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
A bidding war for TDK’s hard-disk drive parts business could determine the prospects of Japanese corporate icon Toshiba as well as who controls an increasingly lucrative artificial intelligence data-center storage market.

Seagate Technology Holdings and delisted Toshiba are vying for TDK’s magnetic-heads business in a deal that could be worth several billion dollars. The winning bidder would be able to expand in-house capabilities in the $23 billion hard-drive market that’s been transformed by voracious AI data-center demand.

Fast-moving AI data-center operators now are demanding hard-drive suppliers pack ever more storage into limited spaces. Prices are climbing and net income at Seagate and Western Digital — which together control more than 90% of the global HDD market, according to research firm TrendForce — has grown by multiples in recent quarters.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: Seagate Technology Holdings and Toshiba are vying for TDK’s magnetic-heads business. The winning bidder would be able to expand in-house capabilities in the $23 billion hard-drive market.

https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.title: EU takes firmer stance on China’s trade practices as Beijing talks begin
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.author: No Author
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.text:
The European Union is striking a more assertive approach to China as it heads into two days of negotiations in Beijing aimed at avoiding an economically damaging trade war.

The EU’s trade chief, Maros Sefcovic, is set to meet with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao this week to address a trade deficit that exceeds $1 billion a day. The meeting comes as the EU prepares what are described as safeguard measures that would limit imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles — a move that may be seen as an escalation.

Germany and France this week called on the EU to adopt stronger tools — including an instrument that could cut off China from the bloc’s massive single market — in order to defend European sectors that have fallen prey to surging Chinese imports. But the EU wants to moderate its action to try to avoid retaliation from Beijing.
https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/20.summary: EU's trade chief Maros Sefcovic is set to meet with Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao this week. Meeting comes as the EU prepares what are described as safeguard measures that would limit imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles.

https://www.dw.com/en/man-injured-after-.title: Man injured after New York shooting involving ICE
https://www.dw.com/en/man-injured-after-.text:
The shooting happened in the afternoon in the Bronx, with details still emerging. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the incident and urged Donald Trump to end ICE actions in the city.

A man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent during an arrest, New York City metropolitan police said Thursday.

The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. local time (2100 GMT) in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx, which is one of New York's five boroughs.

Details are still emerging, but the New York Police Department has denied that its personnel were involved in the shooting.

"The individual who was shot is at a nearby hospital and is currently conscious and receiving medical attention," the NYPD said in a statement.

US President Donald Trump's administration has scaled up ICE raids in major US cities to detain and deport people who are in the US illegally.

Local media in New York said ICE was involved in the latest shooting in the Bronx, which has sparked protests.

New York City Zohran Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he contacted President Trump.

"This is an unconscionable and incredible serious situation," Mamdani said in a post on X. "I have called the President; when we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agent terrorize our communities.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul earlier said she has been briefed on the incident.

"We expect federal authorities to provide a full and transparent accounting of the circumstances surrounding the incident," Hochul said in a statement posted on X.

"New Yorkers deserve to know exactly what happened and why."

The Department of Homeland Security is the parent agency of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). In a post on X, DHS said the person who was shot was a "criminal illegal alien from the Dominican Republic" with "associations to the Trinitarios gang."

DHS said an ICE officer "discharged his weapon" during the incident and said ICE officers immediately rendered aid after the man was injured. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital," the statement added, while mentioning that the FBI is on the scene.

Deadly ICE and Border Patrol shootings have drawn major controversy during Trump's second term, particularly regarding the training and oversight of the agents.

An ICE agent killed a 37-year-old US citizen, Renee Good, during their operations in Minnepolis in January, triggering demonstrations there and in several other US cities.

Later that month, Alex Pretti, another US citizen, was killed by two US Customs and Border Protection officers agents in Minneapolis following an altercation.

https://www.dw.com/en/us-to-livestream-f.title: US to livestream Fort Hood shooter's execution: Pentagon
https://www.dw.com/en/us-to-livestream-f.text:
US Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth had said that Nidal Hasan would be executed by firing squad and that it would be done "in public." Hasan's execution will be the first by the US military since 1961.

The execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, who shot and killed 13 people at Ford Hood in 2009, will be livestreamed, the US military said Thursday.

The confirmation came a day after US Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth had said Hasan's execution, which is slated for December 3, would be done in "public."

Pentagon officials added that more details on the execution would follow.

In a video posted on X by official Pentagon accounts, Hegseth had said Wednesday that Hasan would get "a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be, and we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public."

Hegseth was speaking to right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec on board the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier, which ended a nearly 10-month deployment on Thursday.

"People need to understand that there's serious consequence for these types of things," Hegseth said.

Hasan's execution will be the first by the US military since 1961, and will be the first to be done by firing squad since World War II.

Hegseth added: "I kind of like the mentality we had in World War II, which was win."

US Army psychiatrist Hasan killed 13 people and wounded 32 others at Fort Hood, Texas.

A military court sentenced him to death in 2013.

During his trial, Hasan said he had perpetrated the shooting to protect Taliban members in Afghanistan from US troops.

The announcement that Hasan will be executed by firing squad comes amid the fallout of the botched execution of Christa Pike.

https://www.dw.com/en/ex-german-chancell.title: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
https://www.dw.com/en/ex-german-chancell.text:
Former Chancellor Gerhard Schröder still maintains a friendship with Russian leader Vladimir Putin. Tensions are high between Germany and Russia as the invasion of Ukraine continues.

Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder attended Russian President Vladimir Putin's birthday party, the Kremlin said Thursday.

Putin celebrated his 74th birthday in Moscow on Wednesday. The Kremlin said Putin learned that Schröder was on a business trip in the Russian capital via Russian media reports.

"The president invited his old friend to his home," the Kremlin said, with the Russian government releasing pictures of Schröder and Putin smiling and clasping hands.

Schröder, who is 82 years old, was in Moscow visiting one of the branches of the new Hyperglobus supermarket chain. The ex-German chancellor was named to the chain's supervisory board last week.

Hyperglobus was originally part of German retail company Globus Holding, which operates the Globus supermarkets in Germany and the Czech Republic.

Globus Holding also had supermarkets in Russia, but divested its stake last year, with those stores thus being spun off into seperate company Hyperglobus.

Schröder, a member of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), served as Germany's chancellor from 1998 to 2005.

Since leaving the chancellery, Schröder has worked for Russian state-owned energy firms and has also maintained personal contact with Putin.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Schröder's fondness for Russia has drawn controversy, particularly since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Schröder's tax-payer financed Berlin office was closed in 2022 over his involvement in the Russian energy sector, and he has also faced calls by fellow party members to be expelled from the SPD.

Schröder, however, has survived the attempt to be kicked out of his party.

Friedrich Merz is the 10th chancellor of the Federal Republic of Germany. He is also the chairman of Germany's center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Merz, a former European Parliament lawmaker and commercial lawyer who was born in 1955, hails from a rural area of Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia. He is a staunch Catholic and made a career in business

Olaf Scholz took over as German chancellor, after having served as finance minister and vice chancellor for three years. The conservative and soft-spoken Social Democrat displayed stoicism and unwavering self-confidence. The former mayor of Hamburg looked back on a decades-long political career, which included a number of upsets.

Angela Merkel was elected Germany’s first female chancellor. Through her pragmatic style of leadership, she successfully sidelined competitors within her party and navigated through numerous crises over 16 years in government.

After Helmut Kohl’s fourth term in office, German voters were in a mood for change. Gerhard Schröder became chancellor in the first coalition of SPD and environmentalist Greens. For the first time, German armed forces were deployed abroad under a NATO mandate, including to Afghanistan. Schröder's reorganization of the welfare system, the so-called Agenda 2010, became a real test for his party.

His term lasted 16 years. For many years, Helmut Kohl was seen as sitting things out, in an unflinching, patient style, with no particular interest in big reforms. But his big historic achievement stands in stark contrast to this: German reunification and reconstruction of the former GDR. Kohl was not only the Chancellor of German Unity — he also pushed for further European integration.

Helmut Schmidt took over as chancellor after Willy Brandt resigned. In the face of inflation and economic stagnation, Schmidt’s style was fact-oriented and efficient. He took a hard stance towards the left-wing extremist group Red Army Faction (RAF). He had to step down as a result of a no-confidence vote in parliament when his coalition partner, the FDP switched allegiances.

Social upheaval in Germany led to a change in politics, with Willy Brandt becoming the first Social Democratic chancellor. He kneeled before the memorial in the former Warsaw Ghetto — a historic gesture of seeking forgiveness for Nazi cruelty and a sign of reconciliation. He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1971 for his contribution to easing tensions with countries in the East.

Kurt Georg Kiesinger forged Germany’s first "grand coalition" between the CDU and SPD. The government managed to add new impetus to the country’s stagnating economy. Kiesinger’s membership in Adolf Hitler's NSDAP party became the subject of heated debate. In 1968, Beate Klarsfeld publicly slapped him in the face during the 1968 Christian Democrat convention calling him a Nazi.

In 1963, the CDU urged 87-year-old Adenauer to step down. Ludwig Erhard was chosen as his successor, having earned some popularity as minister of economics. He supported social economics and become the "father" of the west-German economic boom. He was rarely seen without a cigar in his mouth and is said to have smoked 15 per day. In 1966, Erhard stepped down as chancellor.

Konrad Adenauer was the first German chancellor. During his term in office, the young federal republic became a sovereign state, with foreign policies looking towards the west. His style of governing was seen as authoritarian. Adenauer was from the Rhineland region and pushed for Bonn to become the German capital. But he was never a great fan of the Rhineland's popular Carnival tradition.

https://www.dw.com/en/uk-two-latvian-men.title: UK: Two Latvian men arrested for breaking into RAF base
https://www.dw.com/en/uk-two-latvian-men.text:
The men were arrested for breaching a perimeter fence at a UK air base that houses US and NATO intelligence operations. The incident comes after an alleged terror plot at another air base in England was foiled recently.

Two Latvian men have been arrested for breaching the perimeter fence at an RAF base used by the US military, UK police said Thursday.

The two UK residents, aged 36 and 32, were arrested by counterterrorism police at the Royal Air Force (RAF) Molesworth base in southeastern England, 70 miles north of London.

Police said they were being held on suspicion of trespassing, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place "for a purpose prejudicial to the UK."

A former World War II airbase, RAF Molesworth, is now a non-flying facility that is managed by the US Air Force.

It houses intelligence personnel from US Africa Command and the NATO Intelligence Fusion Center, which provides information to the Supreme Allied Commander in Europe.

The incident comes after several men were arrested amid an alleged terror plot at another UK air base last month.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

According to a statement from Counter Terrorism Policing London, officers from the Ministry of Defense Police and Cambridgeshire Constabulary began investigating an incident at approximately 10 p.m. local time on Wednesday after an abandoned vehicle was found near the edge of the base.

Police later discovered a small hole in the perimeter fence and arrested the two suspects at around 2 a.m. on Thursday.

The men were initially arrested on suspicion of trespassing on a prohibited site and criminal damage. They were later arrested on charges of entering a prohibited place with the intent to harm the UK.

Both men remain in police custody. Due to the nature of the offense, the matter is being investigated by counterterrorism police.

On September 27, authorities discovered three suspicious vans near RAF Fairford, a British air base from which US bombers launched strikes against Iran. This triggered a widespread investigation that led to seven arrests.

Last weekend, the US Air Force brought home all the bombers deployed to the base.

Commander Helen Flanagan, head of the counterterrorism unit, said that while UK authorities are "very aware of the recent heightened interest and concern around military sites", there is "nothing to suggest" the incident at RAF Molesworth is related to what happened at RAF Fairford last week, although she added that the investigation was still in its "very early stages."

The US European Command acknowledged the incident but declined to comment on specific force protection measures.

https://www.dw.com/en/afghan-women-facin.title: Afghan women facing arrest for dress code violations: UN
https://www.dw.com/en/afghan-women-facin.text:
In recent months, the Taliban authorities in Afghanistan have arrested or detained dozens of women for alleged violations of dress codes and for appearing in public without a male guardian.

At least 52 women and one girl were arrested or detained in the Afghan cities of Herat and Kabul between July and September of 2026, according to a statement released by the United Nations on Thursday.

"Women were detained for not wearing a chador [an all-enveloping, cloak-like garment], having visible hair, wearing colourful scarves or makeup, or being in public without a mahram [male chaperone]," the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) said.

According to the mission, the detained women were released after being held for several hours. It also warned that the number of cases could be higher due to underreporting.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

UNAMA said it was "gravely concerned" by the arrests, detentions, and threats of arrest.

The mission stated that the detentions violate women's and girls' rights to freedom of movement, expression, and autonomy. The detentions also expose them to severe social stigma in traditional Afghan society, UNAMA said.

In June, Afghan authorities opened fire on a rare protest in Herat over the arrests and detentions of women for alleged dress code violations. According to witnesses and the UN mission, at least one person was killed and several others were injured.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Since seizing power in 2021 as US-led forces withdrew from Afghanistan, the Taliban government has imposed severe restrictions on women and girls, including banning them from attending school beyond the primary level and limiting what they can wear and where they can go.

In public, women must wear a full hijab, which includes a headscarf, a long robe that covers the body, and a face covering. The Ministry for the Propagation of Virtue and the Prevention of Vice enforces these rules.

Earlier this week, the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued four arrest warrants for senior Taliban officials, accusing them of committing crimes against humanity by systematically depriving women and girls in Afghanistan of their rights.

Hovewer, the Taliban rejected the decision, calling it a politically motivated violation of Afghanistan's sovereignty.

https://www.dw.com/en/us-suspends-micros.title: US suspends Microsoft, Adobe from filing for green cards
https://www.dw.com/en/us-suspends-micros.text:
The Trump administration cut off tech firms, including Microsoft and Adobe, from filing for green cards for their foreign workers.

The Trump administration on Thursday said it was suspending major tech firms, including Microsoft, from applying for a program that allowed their foreign workers to work permanently in the US.

US Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling accused those tech firms of abusing the program — the Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM) — that had so far been a legal pathway for workers to apply for green cards.

"I am hereby suspending from the Permanent Labor Certification Program some of the largest IT outsourcing firms in the world, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL, and Capgemini," US Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said.

Sonderling said the suspensions were due to ongoing federal investigations into those firms.

There are good reasons that Indian media firms covered the issue so urgently because many of those firms are either Indian or rely on thousands of Indian professionals who've moved to the country.

Vice President JD Vance said the PERM system required companies to advertise work in the US before they applied for green cards for foreign workers due to a lack of qualified American job applicants.

"They'll put an advertisement in a small-town newspaper. They'll go out there and say that 'We have advertised for a position with our company, and nobody is responding to it.' And they will use that lack of response to then go and replace American workers with what is effectively foreign indentured servants," Vance claimed.

"There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has used this system more than Microsoft," Vance said.

The announcement came hours before US President Donald Trump was scheduled to award the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.

Microsoft said in a statement that it looked forward to providing the administration with additional information, saying the majority of its workers are Americans and that a large part of the H-1B filings have to do with the status of people already based in the US.

"We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings," the company said.

The H-1B visa program is another part of the Trump administration's crackdown on immigration, as concerns have long persisted that the visa for skilled workers has displaced Americans in favor of lower-cost foreign labor.

Microsoft employs 125,000 US workers and 103,000 international workers, according to the company's 2025 annual report.

https://www.dw.com/en/south-africa-anti-.title: South Africa: Anti-migrant protests turn violent
https://www.dw.com/en/south-africa-anti-.text:
A court order requiring the government to resume processing asylum applications reignited violent protests against immigration in South Africa.

Anti-migrant protests erupted in South Africa on Thursday as tensions over immigration were reignited by a court order requiring the government to resume processing asylum applications.

Some of the protests turned violent, according to local media reports. This included incidents in the coastal city of Durban and the Soweto township of Johannesburg, where cars were set on fire and gunshots were heard.

The unrest in Durban reportedly followed a protest by a group demanding that a refugee center stop processing asylum applications. About 10 vehicles were overturned and set on fire. Foreign-owned shops were also looted.

Meanwhile, in Soweto, residents clashed with foreign shop owners, and gunshots were heard, according to the broadcaster Newzroom Afrika.

At least nine vehicles were torched, said Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department spokesman Superintendent Xolani Fihla in an interview with SABC television.

"It's reported that there were clashes between foreign nationals in the area and South African nationals," he said. "At the present moment, I can confirm that no injuries have been reported."

The court ruling that sparked the flare-up of xenophobic tensions deemed certain provisions of the government's refugee policy to be unconstitutional.

The court explained that this was because the provisions prevented individuals from accessing the asylum system on procedural grounds, such as entering the country illegally.

Recently, this ruling has led hundreds of people, reportedly including those who do not qualify for asylum, to flock to government refugee centers.

On Wednesday, the government emphasized that the judgement "does not grant refugee status or permanent residence automatically to anyone who enters South Africa."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

South Africa has experienced months of anti-immigrant protests this year. Populist and anti-immigrant groups have demanded that undocumented foreign nationals leave by June 30.

Amidst international criticism, tens of thousands of people have fled the country, while some were repatriated by their governments.

Although South Africa has a third of its population unemployed, it remains the largest economy in Africa and continues to attract migrants.

Migrants are often blamed for taking jobs, fueling crime, and straining public services. However, social scientists have said these accusations are not supported by evidence.

https://www.dw.com/en/us-will-not-resume.title: US will not resume strikes on Iran before midterms — Trump
https://www.dw.com/en/us-will-not-resume.text:
President Donald Trump said the US will not resume strikes on Iran before the midterm elections on November 3. High gas and grocery prices are top concerns for voters.

US President Donald Trump said he will not order a resumption of military strikes on Iran before the November 3 midterm elections.

Trump's announcement on social media on Thursday came after two US media outlets reported that he was weighing options to strike Iran.

The Atlantic magazine reported  that the thinking was Trump would want to maintain the period of relative calm in the war with Iran until after the elections to keep the deeply unpopular war out of the news. The US has not struck the country in recent weeks.

A Pentagon official told Axios that the Department of Defense's job was to be ready for possible strikes on Iran if the president ordered them.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The US and Iran agreed to a ceasefire agreement in April, but that agreement didn't hold as both countries resumed fighting in the months that followed.

Trump said at the UN General Assembly that he could yet escalate the war with Iran.

But gas and fuel prices remain high in the US, with many voters already feeling the pressure of high prices for groceries and other goods — factors that have weighed on candidates in Trump's Republican Party.

Plus, the economy remains one of the top concerns for voters this midterm, when US citizens are going to be electing members of Congress.

In his social media post on Thursday, Trump also said his team has been "having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran."

That came after Trump, at the end of September, publicly rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — the vital waterway through which a fifth of the world's oil once flowed — to commercial shipping if the US met necessary conditions.

Then Iran last week said it had received a counterproposal.

Trump's post also came as the military dispatched more resources to the Middle East, according to a report the Wall Street Journal.

US officials said a third aircraft-carrier strike group, and its thousands of troops, would arrive by the end of November, according to the newspaper.
